slot.brief: Given three vectors, compute the scalar triple product [a b c] and identify a property (volume, coplanarity) from it

stem: For $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}$, $\vec{b}=\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}=2\hat{i}+\hat{k}$, evaluate $[\vec{a}\vec{b}\vec{c}]$ and state whether the vectors are coplanar.

verdicts.working: \(\vec b\times\vec c=(1,2,-2)\), so \([\vec a\vec b\vec c]=\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)=1+4=5\ne0\). Thus the vectors are not coplanar.

working:
$[vec{a}vec{b}vec{c}]=vec{a}cdot(vec{b}timesvec{c})$.
$vec{b}timesvec{c}=hat{i}+2hat{j}-2hat{k}$.
$[vec{a}vec{b}vec{c}]=(1,2,0)cdot(1,2,-2)=5ne0$.
Hence, the vectors are not coplanar.

Independent check: \(\vec b\times\vec c=(1,2,-2)\), so \([\vec a\vec b\vec c]=\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)=1+4=5\ne0\). Thus the vectors are not coplanar.
solution:
The scalar triple product is $[\vec a\vec b\vec c]=\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)$, and $\vec b\times\vec c=(1,2,-2)$. 
$$[\vec a\vec b\vec c]=(1,2,0)\cdot(1,2,-2)=5\ne0$$
Since the scalar triple product is nonzero, the vectors are not coplanar.
